title: review: H7: normalized failure signatures stop unchanged repeats, failure kinds (code, invalid spec, flaky, environment, conflict, quota, permissions) are classified and routed, and codex_reply resumes only when the worktree is compatible
spec:
Build on goal/T-0353 after H5b (the previous daemon.py change). Handover section 8. Evidence (scout T-0355): daemon.auto_fix_hold_key dedupes on the held_at timestamp, not a content signature, so an unchanged failure can get another round until the lineage cap; only gate_red vs review request_changes are distinguished (merge.py separately flags conflict, tests_red, diff_unavailable); executor.codex_reply checks the thread exists and executor availability only, never that the worktree still matches the thread's last commit.
1. daemon.failure_signature(task) -> str: sha12 over sorted failing test ids (from resume_hint.failures, timestamps and durations stripped), sorted (path, normalized issue text without line numbers and digits) of rejecting review comments, and the failure kind. Stored on each fix round as constraints.failure_signature. auto_fix_round: when the new hold's signature equals any earlier signature in the lineage, do not create a round; escalate with reason "unchanged failure repeated" (hold key as today). A changed signature is never suppressed.
2. daemon.failure_kind(task, worktree) -> one of code_defect, invalid_spec, flaky, environment, conflict, quota, permissions, unknown, from deterministic markers: merge status conflict -> conflict; ModuleNotFoundError, "No module named", ENOENT on tools, missing venv -> environment; EACCES/permission denied/sandbox -> permissions; cooling or usage-limit reasons -> quota; a gate_red whose failing ids all pass on one immediate rerun of only those ids -> flaky (record both runs in resume_hint); review comments that say the spec is contradictory or impossible (markers "spec", "acceptance cannot") -> invalid_spec; else code_defect. Routing: code_defect -> routine fix round (as today); flaky -> one rerun, then escalate with kind; environment, permissions, invalid_spec -> escalate with kind, no round; conflict -> escalate with the T-0258 rebase-task hint; quota -> hold without round or notification spam. The kind is written to pipeline.failure_kind and included in the fix-round packet and the escalation notify text.
3. executor.codex_reply: before resuming a thread, check the worktree HEAD equals the commit recorded when the thread last ended (store it on the task as codex_thread_head when a thread finishes) or is its descendant, and the tree is clean; otherwise start a fresh thread with a compact repair packet (spawn.packet plus the delta) and record resume_incompatible: reason on the task. Never resume with a stale thread id after the worktree moved.
4. pool.toml [daemon]: auto_fix_rounds stays; add flaky_rerun_max = 1 and document the kinds.
Tests: tests/test_daemon.py::test_unchanged_failure_signature_escalates_instead_of_new_round, ::test_changed_signature_gets_a_round, ::test_failure_kind_environment_escalates_without_round, ::test_flaky_rerun_then_escalate, ::test_quota_hold_creates_no_round; tests/test_executor.py::test_codex_reply_fresh_thread_when_worktree_moved, ::test_codex_reply_resumes_when_compatible. Keep every existing test green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; git add -A and commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: every fix round created by auto_fix_round carries constraints.failure_signature and the held task carries pipeline.failure_kind
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

Acceptance criterion 1 cannot pass.

Neither test_codex_reply_fresh_thread_when_worktree_moved nor test_codex_reply_resumes_when_compatible exists, and the diff doesn't add them, so acceptance criterion 2 cannot pass despite _resume_compatible being implemented.

The flaky-rerun subprocess.run(['pytest','-q',*ids], cwd=worktree, capture_output=True, text=True) call has no timeout, unlike every other subprocess dispatch in this module which goes through _run(..., timeout, ...). A hanging test blocks the whole daemon tick indefinitely, violating the module's documented invariant that timeouts are always enforced by the spawner.
